answer: The summit lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the ripple is where a second reviewer recomputes them. The design leans on time-locked work history, published publicly on failure, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. Written in a short declarative sentences register, it stays short. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the umber of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
